If you're curious about what it might feel like to be a hacker in the early days of the internet, and you enjoy solving simple challenges, then I fully recommend this game. It's story-driven, though once you have the tools you can just mess around (at least until you run out of unhacked devices). There's a lot of fun little details, like chat logs on the computers you hack, hidden easter eggs, etc. The graphics are simple and pleasing, and the soundtrack is amazing, it really completes the feeling of being a super-secret hacker. For 10 bucks, this game is worth the money, you'll have an amazing time (and a few stressful times too!). Also, there's a command to open the cd tray. Sadly I don't have one :(, but the command does work!

Visual mess of nodes as you progress, odd keyboard behaviour[1], very restricted set of commands and limited terminal behaviour let this down. Before disconnecting you will always be going to the log folder and deleting all, a tedious activity when on an actual terminal you would have a script, alias the disconnect command or use a semi-colon to run multiple commands on one-line e.g. "cd /log; rm *; dc". However in hacknet you either have to run each command one at a time, either by typing them in or using the janky arrow navigation of history.

[1] Down arrow works fine but up arrow randomly acts as if pressed multiple times. Confirmed with two different keyboards

Hacknet is a hacking simulator. It's a fun, slightly confusing time, and I have enjoyed my time in it thus far thoroughly.

Let me start by saying that this isn't for everyone. It isn't the best at explaining what you need to do at times, and gameplay can become just a bit tedious. You basically spend your time slouched in a chair typing words and hoping they work.

Graphics are irrelevant here, and the price is at a good rate.

My major gripe is that it is either entirely clear what you need to do, while, at other points, it really isn't.

All in all, it's a good game for the price, and I recommend you pick it up.

Probably the most fun you can legally have with directory commands. Still, Hacknet may or may not be for you, depending on what you're hoping to get out of it. 

If you're in it for the narrative experience and the voyeuristic joy of poking around in other people's business and/or places that you don't belong, indulging the cinematically-improbable-but-evergreen-cool Hacker Man(tm) in your heart to the appropriately driving beat of smooth EDM, then you'll definitely enjoy what this game is -- regardless of your actual level of familiarity with all things tech. It's a game that intends to be accessible so it glosses over the hard stuff, handing you tools that amount to pegs you've got to put into the proper holes at the proper time, often under (mild) time pressure. They're basic, familiar video game mechanics, dressed up this time as Hacker Stuff, and I think it works because it takes a back seat to the story. The game doesn't take itself too seriously, but has poignant moments all the same. 

If what you want instead is a game that's going to have you actually writing code or cracking difficult puzzles, this isn't what you're looking for. The guy who made it clearly has a background in tech, but this isn't a Zachtronics thing -- it's essentially a slick visual novel with some fun exploratory/investigative elements and some hidden surprises for diligent snoopers.

I was excited to see that other people have crafted their own bite-sized stories for Hacknet, and I'm looking forward to trying them out!
